newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MATRA CLOSE TO GET HUNGARY MISSILE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: MATRA CLOSE TO GET HUNGARY MISSILE DEAL.

text.p: Hungary has chosen French company Matra Defense as the prime candidate to supply shoulder-launched anti-aircraft missiles worth some $100 million but runners-up are set to contest the decision, a ministry spokesman said on Thursday
"The deal has not yet been signed, but Matra will be the one with which we will continue negotiations," Defence Ministry spokesman Lajos Erdelyi told Reuters.
Hungary, eyeing NATO membership, started last year the process of selecting the supplier for the anti-aircraft missiles and five companies were invited for the second round of bidding.
These were Bombardier unit Short Brothers of Northern Ireland, Hughes Electronics, Sweden's Bofors, France's Matra and Germany's Daimler-Benz .

Tamas Wachsler, member of the parliament's defence committee, said Bofors approached him in a move to contest the decision, but as the race was very close between the two leading bidders, he did not find this surprising.
"I think Matra would have done the same in the opposite case," Wachsler said.
The chairman of the committee, Imre Mecs, told Reuters he has no indication of irregularity in the process.
"According to the report I received from committee members overseeing the process, everything was regular," Mecs said.
He added that the procurement subcommittee will look into the tender next Tuesday and the defence committee will give its final appraisal of the tender on Wednesday.
He also said that as with other procurement tenders, dissatisfaction of the losers is "a matter of course".
Erdelyi shared his view and added that the measure of dissatisfaction is not unusual.

Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti announced at a staff meeting on Tuesday that a ministry panel decided eight to three in favour of Matra. Mecs said that although Keleti's move was not irregular in itself, he was not happy about it.
"It would have been more fortunate if he had notified us (the committee) beforehand," Mecs said.
Official figures for the deal are yet to be announced, but a trade ministry official said in February it would be in the range of $100 million.
Erdelyi said the ministry did not wish to disclose any figure before the deal is completed but would do so as soon as it goes through.

Hungary will shortly prepare an international tender for uprading its radar system -- a deal of similar magnitude to the rocket purchase -- and an $700 million to $800 million tender for some 30 fighter jets.
